title: Controlled vs uncontrolled inputs
objectives: Wire a controlled input by pairing value from state with an onChange that writes e.target.value
Predict what an input with value but no onChange does: a frozen field plus a React warning
Choose an uncontrolled input (defaultValue plus a ref) when you only need the value on submit
Spot the uncontrolled-to-controlled warning and fix it by keeping value defined from the first render

sources.title: React docs: Manipulating the DOM with Refs

questions.prompt: What makes an <input> a controlled component in React?

options.text: Its value comes from state via `value`, and `onChange` writes every change back to state
It has an `onChange` handler, regardless of `value`

questions.explanation: Controlled = React state owns the value. You pass the current value in with `value` and push every keystroke back to state with `onChange`. The two are a pair: `value` alone (no `onChange`) makes the field read-only and triggers a warning; `onChange` alone without `value` is just an uncontrolled input with a listener.

questions.prompt: You render `<input value={query} />` with no `onChange`. What happens when the user types?

options.text: Nothing changes on screen and React warns you supplied `value` without `onChange`
It updates normally — `value` tracks the DOM automatically
The input updates but `query` stays stale

questions.explanation: With `value` set to a state variable that never changes, React re-renders the input back to that fixed value on every keystroke, so the field appears frozen (effectively read-only). React warns that you provided `value` without `onChange` (unless you meant `readOnly`). Add `onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)}` to make it controlled.

questions.prompt: When is an uncontrolled input (`defaultValue` + a ref) a reasonable choice?

options.text: When you only need the value at a single moment (e.g. on submit) and don't need to react to each keystroke
When you want to validate or filter as the user types
Never — every input should be controlled

questions.explanation: Uncontrolled inputs let the DOM own the value; you read it from a ref on demand. That's a fine fit when you only care about the final value (form submit), for file inputs (which are always uncontrolled), or to avoid a re-render per keystroke. If you need to react as the user types — live filtering, validation, enabling a button — go controlled.

prompts.prompt: Wire up a controlled text input bound to the `query` state.
prompts.explanation: A controlled input pairs `value={query}` with `onChange`, and the new text lives at `e.target.value`. Together they keep React state as the single source of truth for the field.

prompts.prompt: Seed the state so `value` is never undefined, avoiding the uncontrolled-to-controlled warning when `user.name` is missing.
prompts.explanation: If `user.name` is `undefined`, `value` starts undefined (uncontrolled) and becomes a string later (controlled) — React warns. Coalescing to `""` with `??` (or `||`) keeps `value` a defined string from the first render, so the input is controlled its whole life.

code: // user starts as {} then updates to { name: "Ada" } after a fetch
snippets.question: What warning does React log when `user.name` goes from undefined to a string?
snippets.answer: A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled.
acceptable: changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled
snippets.explanation: On the first render `user.name` is undefined, so `value={undefined}` makes the input uncontrolled. Once the data loads, `value` becomes a string and the input flips to controlled — React warns: "A component is changing an uncontrolled input to be controlled." Fix it by keeping `value` always defined: `useState(user.name ?? "")`.
